package_info.package_versions: 5.3.0 to 5.3.17, 5.2.0 to 5.2.19, and older unsupported versions (as per CVE-2022-22965)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the spring-web package contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (SpringShell/Spring4Shell, CVE-2022-22965) that allows attackers to exploit class property binding in Spring MVC and Spring WebFlux applications running on JDK 9+ to achieve arbitrary code execution.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes HTTP request parameters that can be mapped to internal class properties, allowing an attacker to set the logging pattern or other internal fields, which can be abused to write a web shell or execute arbitrary code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to bind arbitrary HTTP parameters to internal Java class properties is highly dangerous, especially when it allows modification of classLoader or pipeline fields.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects only safe, whitelisted properties to be set via HTTP parameters. This vulnerability allows attackers to set sensitive internal properties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Property binding is legitimate for user input mapping in web forms, but not for internal classLoader or pipeline fields.
key_indicators: Binding of HTTP parameters to internal Java class properties
No restriction on property names, allowing access to classLoader and pipeline
Ability to write files or change logging patterns via crafted requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request with parameters targeting internal class properties (e.g., class.module.classLoader.resources.context.parent.pipeline.first.pattern).
attack_chain.leads_to: Modification of internal server configuration, such as log pattern or file location.

attack_chain.action: Server processes the request and binds the malicious parameters to internal fields, enabling the attacker to write a web shell or arbitrary file to the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution or web shell deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected changes to server log patterns or file locations at runtime
Creation of new files (e.g., JSP web shells) in web application directories
file_indicators: Unexpected JSP or other executable files appearing in web root directories
Modified log files or log configuration files
network_indicators: Unusual HTTP POST requests with deeply nested parameter names
Outbound connections from the server after exploitation (e.g., C2 callbacks)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP traffic for suspicious parameter names targeting internal Java class properties, especially those related to classLoader, pipeline, or logging. Use file integrity monitoring to detect new or modified files in web application directories. Employ runtime security monitoring to detect changes in log configuration or unexpected file writes by the application process.
